candidate.answerReason: The signed differences around the five people must balance. Their magnitudes split uniquely into equal totals as {19,4} and {7,5,11}. Of the two resulting orientations, only one gives whole-dollar amounts, namely (21,2,9,14,10).

methods.label: Balance the increases and decreases
methods.explanation:
Let \(A,B,C,D,E\) be the five amounts in dollars, in the order given. Going from Ashley to Betty to Carlos to Dick to Elgin and back to Ashley returns to the starting amount, so
\[
(B-A)+(C-B)+(D-C)+(E-D)+(A-E)=0.
\]
The magnitudes of these five differences are \(19,7,5,4,11\), whose sum is 46. Therefore the positive differences and the negative differences must each have total magnitude 23.

The group containing 19 needs another 4 to reach 23. The only way to supply that 4 is the difference of magnitude 4 itself. Thus the two groups must be
\[
19+4=7+5+11=23.
\]
Choosing which group is positive gives exactly two cases.

If \(B-A=19\), the differences force
\[
(A,B,C,D,E)=(t,t+19,t+12,t+7,t+11).
\]
Their total is \(5t+49=56\), giving \(t=7/5\), which is not a whole number.

If \(B-A=-19\), all the signs reverse, giving
\[
(A,B,C,D,E)=(t,t-19,t-12,t-7,t-11).
\]
Now \(5t-49=56\), so \(t=21\). The amounts are consequently
\[
(21,2,9,14,10).
\]
They are nonnegative whole numbers, sum to 56, and have all five required absolute differences. Elgin had \(\boxed{\$10}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
methods.levelReason: The solution uses signed differences, a complete two-case analysis, and linear equations with whole-number restrictions.

candidate.annotationRationale: The task asks for amounts subject to simultaneous integer restrictions. The method exhausts the possible signs of the absolute differences through their balanced totals, then uses integrality to select the valid assignment. Absolute-value simplification and linear equations are supporting knowledge.

review.mathematicalCheck: Cycle closure partitions the difference magnitudes into two totals of 23. The group containing 19 must contain precisely 4, leaving exactly two sign assignments. Their totals give t=7/5 or t=21; only the latter gives whole-dollar amounts, namely (21,2,9,14,10), satisfying every condition.
